one_line: A local-first, voice-operated health diary that exposes its interface actions to an agent through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Nightstand lets users record symptoms and medications, correct or undo entries, adjust accessibility settings, and generate a doctor summary while sharing structured diary state between the human-facing app and an agent.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central rather than decorative: the claimed 19 capabilities mirror the app's actions, enabling hands-free structured entry, correction, undo, accessibility changes, and report generation. A general UI-driving agent could attempt the same flow, but with materially more reliability and interaction friction.
leverage_evidence: Devpost pitch explicitly says every on-screen action is also an agent tool.
Product screenshot visibly claims 19 of 19 capabilities are available to the agent.
Packet describes multi-record logging, correction, undo, accessibility control, and doctor-summary generation by voice.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, intentionally scoped health diary with a consistent local-first UI and a central workflow covering entry, correction, adherence, and reporting. Frame sheets show the app and agent interface in populated states, but the exact end-to-end actions and PDF output are not directly legible or transcript-backed, so execution is not scored in the top band.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show a rendered Nightstand app alongside an agent panel across multiple states.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows Today, History, Medications, Settings, Undo, Edit, and Delete surfaces.
Visible product state includes a knee-pain entry corrected to 5/10 and agent-attributed metadata.
impact_rationale: The project identifies a specific audience—people with conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis who cannot comfortably type—and a real recurring need: maintaining accurate daily records for infrequent clinical consultations. Voice-first logging, repair, accessibility controls, and doctor summaries directly address that need; the packet supports credible value even though live verification is limited.
impact_evidence: About text explains hand pain and stiffness make daily form filling difficult.
The stated workflow supports symptom and medication tracking for doctor consultations.
The packet describes downloadable selectable-text doctor summaries with symptom trends and adherence.
creativity_rationale: The concept is a thoughtful synthesis of voice interaction, local-first health journaling, agent-operated UI, versioned medication schedules, and voice-native repair/undo. Treating correction as a first-class accessibility workflow is a memorable interaction choice, pursued beyond a simple voice form.
creativity_evidence: Voice-native correction and undo are explicitly part of the product concept.
Versioned schedules preserve historical adherence truth.
The app combines agent-operated health records with accessibility controls and clinician-summary generation.
usability_note: The described voice-first and large-control flows fit the target accessibility need; the static evidence cannot fully verify discoverability or error recovery in use.
red_flags: No video transcript is provided despite frame sheets.
Frame text is small and does not clearly expose tool names, payloads, or a complete end-to-end interaction.
Local-only storage and selectable-text PDF claims are not independently verifiable from the packet.
standouts: Strong alignment between the WebMCP mechanism and a concrete accessibility problem.
Repair and undo by voice make shared human-agent state practically useful rather than merely conversational.
Scope includes structured health records, versioned schedules, accessibility settings, and clinician reporting.
advance_reason: A strong, specific accessibility-focused product with substantial WebMCP leverage and credible impact; advance despite incomplete direct execution evidence.
